title: "size at reproductive maturity"
output: html_document
---

```{r}
Lambir_FFR_plantlist <- read.csv(here("size at reproductive maturity", "Lambir_FFR_plantlist.csv"))

Lambir_FFR_phenology <- read.csv(here("size at reproductive maturity", "Lambir_FFR_phenology.csv"))

Lambir_FFR_species <- read.csv(here("size at reproductive maturity", "Lambir_FFR_species.csv"))

```

```{r}
Lambir_merged <- left_join(Lambir_FFR_species, Lambir_FFR_plantlist, by = "spc") %>%
  select(family, genus, species, idno, size)

lambir_final <- left_join(Lambir_merged, Lambir_FFR_phenology, by = "idno") %>%
  select(family, genus, species, idno, size, flw) %>%
  rename( flowers = flw)%>%
  filter(
    !is.na(flowers), #remove rows where not flowering
    !grepl("^\\s*$", flowers), #remove rows wher not flowering
    flowers != "P0", #remove rows where proportion of flowers is 0
    !is.na(size)) %>% #remove rows where no record of size
  mutate(flowers = "flowering") %>% #mark all records as flowering
  distinct() # remove duplicate rows
  
#now remove the idno column because I'm not actually interested in which specific tree was measured
#i just want to know whether a tree was flowering at a certain size

lambir_final_clean <- lambir_final %>%
  select(family, genus, species, size, flowers) %>%
  distinct() %>% #remove duplicate rows
  rename(flowering_at_size_class = size) %>% 
  mutate(binomial_name = paste(genus, species, sep = " ")) %>%
  select (-flowers, -genus, -species) 
```
explanation of size, measures as height in meters

II = 2.5 - 12.5m
III = 12.5 - 27.5m
IV = 27.5 - 42.5m
V > 42.5m


p0 = absent
Pp = less than 25%
P2 = around 50%
P3 = around 75%
P4 = nearly 100%


```{r}
#now see how many of these 189 species are any of the ones that we are interested in
 
species_list <- read.csv(here("species list data", "final species list corrected and cleaned.csv"))

#create a new column with corrected binomial name of each species
species_list$binomial_name <- paste(species_list$genus, species_list$species)

size_at_rep_maturity <- left_join(species_list, lambir_final_clean, by = "binomial_name") %>%   select(binomial_name, family.x, genus, species, history_at_INDFORSUS_site, species_origin, logging_status, flowering_at_size_class) 


size_at_rep_maturity %>%
  filter(!is.na(flowering_at_size_class))

#two species have two records of size at flowering - I want to take the smallest size
#I will need to manually change these

sum(!is.na(size_at_rep_maturity$flowering_at_size_class))
```
